story.title: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

before.rationale: A sandbox or test mode is a fair question for an agentic video tool that can publish to platforms like TikTok, so the axis applies. However, the evidence documents no sandbox, staging, or test environment separate from real data or accounts. Running locally, approving the plan first, and the `--send` flag on post-video are adjacent features, not a documented sandbox capability.

after.rationale: ReelMimic's own `post-video` command runs as a dry run by default, showing what it would post to TikTok/Instagram/YouTube. Actual publishing only happens with an explicit `--send` flag. This lets a user test the publishing step without affecting live accounts, but it is a preview mode rather than a true sandbox environment. Missing for 10: a documented isolated sandbox/test environment, sandbox credentials or test accounts for the platforms, coverage beyond the posting step, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

story.title: As an AI-native user, I can schedule recurring jobs or workflows

before.rationale: Scheduling automation is a fair question for an agentic video-production tool, so the axis applies. The only scheduling evidence is `post-video --at <time>` (reelmimic-gh-9), which schedules a single social-media publish of a finished video. That is an adjacent one-off posting feature, not recurring jobs or workflows. Nothing in the pack shows cron-like or repeating schedules for generation workflows, and resume-after-limit (reelmimic-docs-10) is unrelated.

after.rationale: ReelMimic's own `post-video` CLI accepts `--at <datetime> --tz <zone>`, so a finished video can be scheduled to publish to TikTok, Instagram or YouTube at a set time (gh-9, gh-14). That is one-off timed posting, not recurring jobs. Nothing shows cron-like recurrence or scheduled video-generation workflows. Pause/resume on limits (docs-10) is not scheduling, so it gets no credit. missing for 10: recurring schedules (cron/interval), scheduling of generation jobs or workflows rather than single posts, schedule management (list/edit/cancel), first-party docs and independent corroboration of the scheduling feature.

story.title: As a creator, a character or scene stays consistent across multiple generated shots, not just within one clip

before.rationale: Nothing in the evidence documents keeping a character or scene consistent across multiple generated shots. The closest items don't qualify: Seedance 2.5's 'large reference budget' [runway-docs-3] never claims cross-shot consistency. 'Characters' [runway-docs-7] are conversational avatars and sessions, an adjacent feature, and Brand Kits are a different capability. None of these demonstrate persistent character or scene identity across clips.

after.rationale: Runway's hosted models accept reference inputs: Seedance 2.5 offers a 'large reference budget for images, videos, and audio' and Kling 4.0 generates from 'image or video references'. That is a plausible mechanism for carrying a character or scene across shots, but the evidence never claims cross-shot consistency. The 'Characters' feature is conversational avatars and Brand Kits are a different feature, so neither counts here. Missing for 10: an explicit documented cross-shot character/scene consistency feature, a description of how references keep identity stable across separate generations, and hands-on or independent corroboration of consistency.

story.title: As an AI-native user, I can perform bulk operations across many items at once

before.rationale: Bulk operations are a fair question for a data platform, so the axis applies. However, the evidence has no documented first-party bulk-action capability, such as multi-select actions or batch endpoints for acting on many workspace objects at once. The CLI, SDK and REST APIs are documented for 'automation scripts' and to 'automate Databricks operations', but these are developer building blocks a user could script bulk work with, not a bulk-operation feature itself, so they earn no credit here.

after.rationale: Databricks' core engine processes data in bulk: ANSI SQL with Delta Lake extensions runs over entire tables, batch and streaming computation is supported, and ETL pipelines process whole datasets. The CLI and Python SDK are documented for automating platform operations from scripts, and Unity Catalog objects can be managed through SQL, CLI and REST APIs. However, no evidence shows first-party bulk actions for managing many assets at once (jobs, permissions, catalog objects), so applying an operation to many items appears to require scripting. missing for 10: documented native bulk/batch endpoints or UI actions for operating on many workspace assets at once, AI-agent-driven bulk actions, independent hands-on corroboration.

story.title: As an analyst, a marketplace of third-party datasets lets me enrich my own data directly inside the platform

before.rationale: MotherDuck documents data sharing within an organization and public shares that anyone with a MotherDuck account in the same region can attach, such as a sample hacker_news share. No marketplace or discoverable catalog of third-party datasets is documented. Public share URLs are an adjacent sharing feature, not a dataset marketplace, so they earn no credit for this story.

after.rationale: MotherDuck documents public Shares that anyone with a MotherDuck account in the same cloud region can attach, including users outside the publishing organization. Its docs show attaching a shared dataset (md:_share/hacker_news/...) to analyze it alongside your own data, so third-party data can be consumed inside the platform. However, nothing in the evidence describes a marketplace: no catalog, discovery, listings, or commercial third-party data providers, and no worked enrichment example. Missing for 10: a documented dataset marketplace or catalog with discovery, third-party provider listings, an enrichment workflow, and independent corroboration.

story.title: As an AI-native user, I can schedule recurring jobs or workflows

before.rationale: Reclaim's Habits feature finds and auto-schedules recurring routines on the calendar, and the scheduler flexibly reschedules them when conflicts come up. That covers recurring time blocks, but nothing shows it running recurring automated jobs or multi-step workflows beyond placing calendar events. missing for 10: scheduling recurring jobs/workflows that execute actions (not just calendar blocks), workflow definition or triggers, API/programmatic scheduling, independent hands-on corroboration of recurring automation.

after.rationale: The story asks for recurring automated jobs or workflows, which is a fair automation question for an AI scheduling assistant. However, the evidence only shows Habits and Tasks: recurring, flexible calendar time blocks for the user's own work (reclaim-docs-4, reclaim-docs-31, reclaim-docs-53). That is an adjacent feature, not the ability to schedule jobs or workflows that execute automatically. No cron-style automation, workflow builder or recurring API-triggered job capability is documented.
